why: Holmes says the word band explained what she glimpsed by the light of her match.

text: After his Eastern training, as Holmes reads it: Dr. Roylott has the idea of a poison no chemical test could discover
why: Holmes says such an undetectable poison would occur to a man with an Eastern training.

text: Before the whistles, as Holmes reads it: Dr. Roylott trains the snake, probably with milk, to return when summoned
why: Holmes says he trained it, probably with the milk, to return when summoned.

text: At the hour he thinks best, as Holmes reads it: Dr. Roylott puts the snake through the ventilator
why: Holmes says he would put it through the ventilator at the hour he thought best.

text: As Holmes reads it: the snake crawls down the rope
why: Holmes says it would crawl down the rope.

text: As Holmes reads it: the snake lands on the bed
why: Holmes says it would land on the bed.

text: Before the morning light, as Holmes reads it: Dr. Roylott must recall the snake by the whistle
why: Holmes says he must recall the snake before morning light, in connection with the whistle.

text: Sooner or later, as Holmes reads it: the occupant of the bed falls victim to the snake
why: Holmes says sooner or later she must fall a victim.

text: At Stoke Moran: Holmes reconsiders his position, once it is clear the danger could not come by window or door
why: Holmes says he reconsidered once the danger could not come by window or door, which he tested at the house.

text: At Stoke Moran: Holmes's attention is drawn to the ventilator and the bell-rope
why: Holmes says his attention was drawn to the ventilator and bell-rope, examined at Stoke Moran.

text: At Stoke Moran: Holmes suspects that the rope is a bridge for something coming through the hole to the bed
why: Holmes states the suspicion that the rope was a bridge for something passing through the hole to the bed.

text: At Stoke Moran: the idea of a snake occurs to Holmes
why: Holmes says the idea of a snake instantly occurred to him following those discoveries.

text: At Stoke Moran: Holmes thinks of the whistle
why: Holmes says 'Then I thought of the whistle' in this sequence of reasoning.

text: What was the whistle for? — to call the snake home before the morning light
id: q.whistle_for=to call the snake home before the morning light
why: Holmes explains the whistle recalled the snake before morning light.

text: Why was the whistle heard only during the last few nights? — the snake was being sent each night as the wedding drew near, and called back each time
id: q.why_whistle_began=the snake was being sent each night as the wedding drew near, and called back each time
why: Reasonable inference from Julia's last few nights of whistles, the near wedding and Holmes's account of repeated nightly attempts.

text: Why has the low whistle been heard again now? — the snake is being sent to her now, as it was to her sister
id: q.why_whistle_again=the snake is being sent to her now, as it was to her sister
why: Follows from Helen being moved to the same room and Holmes's explanation.

text: Why did no harm come to Helen last night after the whistle? — the snake was sent that night and did not bite her, as it might not on any night
id: q.helen_unharmed=the snake was sent that night and did not bite her, as it might not on any night
why: Holmes says it might or might not bite the occupant on any night.

text: What, if anything, came through the ventilator into that room? — a venomous snake
why: Holmes has explained the snake came through the ventilator.

text: How was the snake got from the safe to the bed and back? — he put it through the ventilator to crawl down the rope, and whistled it back
id: q.how_snake_worked=he put it through the ventilator to crawl down the rope, and whistled it back
why: Holmes describes the ventilator, rope and whistle; the safe was shown as its den in ¶245-246.

text: How was the snake got from the safe to the bed and back? — the milk or some vibration brought it back, and not the sound of the whistle
id: q.how_snake_worked=the milk or some vibration brought it back, and not the sound of the whistle
why: A fair rival possibility given the milk Holmes mentions and general knowledge about snakes; it reveals no story fact.

text: Why did Julia live on after the bite when Dr. Roylott died within seconds?
why: The story gives Julia's slow death and Roylott's death within ten seconds, so the question arises naturally.

text: Why did Julia live on after the bite when Dr. Roylott died within seconds? — she was bitten somewhere slower to act than the head
id: q.julia_lingered=she was bitten somewhere slower to act than the head
why: A plausible possibility for the discrepancy the story raises.

text: Why did Julia live on after the bite when Dr. Roylott died within seconds? — Holmes's ten seconds is only a manner of speaking
id: q.julia_lingered=Holmes's ten seconds is only a manner of speaking
why: A plausible possibility about Holmes's stated ten seconds.

text: Were there marks of the fangs on Julia that the inquiry missed?
why: Inquiry found no marks, and Holmes says only a sharp-eyed coroner would spot the punctures.

text: Were there marks of the fangs on Julia that the inquiry missed? — two small punctures were there and went unnoticed
id: q.punctures=two small punctures were there and went unnoticed
why: Directly suggested by Holmes's remark about the two little dark punctures.

text: Were there marks of the fangs on Julia that the inquiry missed? — nothing was left that could be seen
id: q.punctures=nothing was left that could be seen
why: A plain alternative, since the inquiry found no marks of violence.

text: What, if anything, came through the ventilator into that room? — came from Dr. Roylott's room, by the ventilator
why: Holmes says it was put through the ventilator from the Doctor's side, the opening communicating with his room.

text: How could anything have reached Julia in a room shut on every side? — through the little opening from Dr. Roylott's room
why: Holmes identifies the hole by the ventilator from Roylott's room as the route.

text: What was the whistle for? — the snake had to be recalled before the morning light revealed it
why: Holmes states the snake had to be recalled before the morning light revealed it.
